```{r Attach packages, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
source("../common/load-neoipcr.R")
load_neoipcr(dev_pkg_path = "../../../neoipcr")
source("../common/helpers.R")
source("../common/logging.R")
suppressMessages(library(tidyverse, warn.conflicts = FALSE, quietly = TRUE))
configure_logging(report = "validation-report")
```

```{r Initialise locale dependent information}
#| include: false

if(!exists("params")) params <- list()

locale <- Sys.getenv("LC_ALL")
localeObj <- parse_locales(locale)[[1]]
invisible(Sys.setlocale(category = "LC_ALL", locale = locale))
invisible(Sys.setLanguage(localeObj$language))
language <- localeObj$language
sR <- get_string_resources(localeObj)

departmentFilter <- params$departmentFilter
support_email_address <- "NeoIPC-Support@charite.de"
```

```{r Data Import}
# No warning/message suppression here: configure_logging() (in the first chunk)
# installs a knitr output hook that routes import_dhis2()'s warnings and messages
# into the unified log channel and keeps them out of the rendered body; a
# `warning=FALSE` here would drop them before the hook can log them.
connection_options <- get_connection_options(
  scheme = params$dhis2Scheme,
  hostname = params$dhis2Hostname,
  port = params$dhis2Port,
  path = params$dhis2Path)

# The import runs without the validation pass: the report is about the records
# that pass would remove, so they have to be kept and validated here — the
# enrolments without an admission form (rule 26) among them, which the
# import's orphan removal otherwise drops. That also includes the patients
# with no enrolment, which rule 1 is about and which only
# `include_unenrolled_patients` keeps in the dataset.
dataset_options <- neoipcr::dhis2_dataset_options(
  department_filter = departmentFilter,
  include_department = "full",
  include_hospital = "full",
  include_country = "full",
  include_world_bank_class = "full",
  include_patient = "full",
  patient_columns = c("id", "sex", "birth_weight", "gestational_age",
                       "delivery_mode", "siblings"),
  include_enrollment = "full",
  include_event = "full",
  include_dhis2_ids = c("departments","patients","enrollments","events"),
  include_incomplete = c("enrollments","events"),
  include_test_data = isTRUE(params$includeTestData),
  include_ineligible_patients = TRUE,
  include_unenrolled_patients = TRUE,
  include_invalid_patients = TRUE,
  locale = locale)

data <- with_error_trace(neoipcr::import_dhis2(
  connection_options = connection_options,
  dataset_options = dataset_options))

# The problem list links each patient record to its Tracker Capture dashboard
# on the instance the data came from: the API base URL with the web context in
# place of the `/api` path, and the program the import resolved by its code.
tracker_capture_url <- httr2::url_parse(connection_options$base_url)
api_path <- tracker_capture_url$path
if (is.null(api_path)) api_path <- ""
tracker_capture_url$path <- paste0(
  sub("/api/?$", "", api_path), "/dhis-web-tracker-capture/index.html")
tracker_capture_base <- httr2::url_build(tracker_capture_url)
NeoIPC_ProgramId <- data$metadata$programId
if (is.null(NeoIPC_ProgramId))
  rlang::abort("The imported metadata carries no program id; the dashboard links cannot be built.")
```

```{r Filter metadata to in-scope departments}
#| include: false

# departmentFilter narrows which departments the validation runs over.
# When NULL, every department returned by import_dhis2 is in scope.
departments <- data$metadata$departments
if (!rlang::is_null(departmentFilter))
  departments <- departments |>
    dplyr::filter(.data$code %in% departmentFilter)
```

```{r Validate}
#| include: false

# The rules live in neoipcr; the sentences that render their findings live
# in this report's string resources, keyed by rule id. A rule the package
# runs without its templates and `summary` here would render as a blank line
# or fail the header below, so every rule is checked for them first: the
# templates are the rule's `description` and, for rule 20, a second complete
# sentence for a pathogen recorded as causing a secondary sepsis.
rule_ids <- neoipcr::validation_rule_ids()
template_keys <- function(rule_id)
  c("description", if (rule_id == 20L) "description_secondary_bsi")
has_text <- function(rule_id) {
  entry <- sR$problems[[as.character(rule_id)]]
  all(vapply(
    c(template_keys(rule_id), "summary"),
    \(field) is.character(entry[[field]]) && length(entry[[field]]) == 1L &&
      nzchar(entry[[field]]),
    logical(1)))
}
unsentenced <- rule_ids[!vapply(rule_ids, has_text, logical(1))]
if (length(unsentenced) > 0L)
  rlang::abort(sprintf(
    "The string resources carry no complete description and summary for validation rule(s) %s.",
    paste(unsentenced, collapse = ", ")))

exceptions <- NULL
if (!is.null(params$validationExceptionFile))
  exceptions <- neoipcr::read_validation_exceptions(params$validationExceptionFile)

# An empty `rules` value (NULL, or `[]` from the command line) means every
# rule; a repeated id is applied once, so the header counts it once. An id
# that is not a whole number is refused here rather than truncated to one.
requested_rules <- unique(unlist(params$rules))
if (length(requested_rules) == 0L) {
  rules <- rule_ids
} else {
  if (!is.numeric(requested_rules) ||
      !all(is.finite(requested_rules) & requested_rules == round(requested_rules)))
    rlang::abort(sprintf(
      "`rules` must name validation rules by their whole-number ids, not %s.",
      paste(requested_rules, collapse = ", ")))
  rules <- as.integer(requested_rules)
}
problems <- neoipcr::validate(data, rules = rules, exceptions = exceptions)

# A rule the package could not run, for want of a column the dataset does not
# hold, flags nothing and would read as clean. This import asks for every
# tier, so such a skip means the dataset is not what the report expects, and
# the render fails rather than presenting the result as complete.
rules_skipped <- attr(problems, "rules_skipped")
if (length(rules_skipped) > 0L)
  rlang::abort(sprintf(
    "Validation rule(s) %s could not be applied to the imported dataset; see the log for the column each is missing.",
    paste(rules_skipped, collapse = ", ")))

# The header says which rules produced this report, so a document rendered
# with a subset cannot be read as a clean bill on the rules it skipped.
rules_not_applied <- setdiff(rule_ids, rules)
rules_applied_text <- if (length(rules_not_applied) == 0L) {
  interpolate_translation(sR$rules_applied_all, count = length(rule_ids))
} else {
  interpolate_translation(
    sR$rules_applied_subset,
    applied     = length(rules),
    total       = length(rule_ids),
    not_applied = paste(
      sprintf(
        "%d (%s)",
        rules_not_applied,
        vapply(
          as.character(rules_not_applied),
          \(id) sR$problems[[id]]$summary,
          character(1))),
      collapse = "; "))
}
rules_applied_text <- as.character(rules_applied_text)
```
